headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: ChatGPT Desktop can read user files/screens while OpenHands can write and exfiltrate broadly, creating unsafe pairwise workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, while OpenHands can use MCP and browser/tool loops. If content from ChatGPT is copied into OpenHands or shared via files, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content is copied into OpenHands without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF OpenHands reads file content originating from ChatGPT Desktop, prompt-like instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy for model outputs.
Strip instructions from shared files before handing them to OpenHands.
Require a human review step before any tool-using action.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and OpenHands can write files and use broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive content can flow from ChatGPT into OpenHands and then out through OpenHands' broader network path. The profiles do not show a blocking isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents access the same project files or copied screenshots, sensitive data can be exposed to OpenHands.
IF OpenHands sends runtime context to external services, leaked content can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste secrets, screenshots, or code into shared channels.
Turn off network access in OpenHands for sensitive tasks.
Use redacted test data only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad runtime execution; ChatGPT Desktop can read files and app context but has no write_filesystem. In a shared repo or mounted volume, OpenHands can overwrite artifacts that ChatGPT later reads, causing direct write/read conflicts and race-prone git state changes. The pair lacks a documented locking mechanism.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or mounted volume, file conflicts are likely.
IF OpenHands commits or rewrites files while ChatGPT Desktop is reading them, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer.
Use separate branches or directories.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Review git diffs before merging.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived conclusions, and OpenHands can act on them with shell, browser, and git capabilities. If OpenHands treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. OpenHands is powerful enough to amplify mistakes, but the profiles do not prove automatic execution without any review.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes ChatGPT output without verification, incorrect facts can become actions.
IF ChatGPT-generated code is applied directly by OpenHands, downstream defects can spread.
mitigations: Require OpenHands to verify claims against source files.
Use a checklist before any commit or shell action.
Ask ChatGPT for citations or diffs, not final actions.
Limit OpenHands to read-only review for high-risk tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while OpenHands handles files in its runtime and model-provider API keys. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into both systems, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in both agents, policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs.
Check vendor retention settings before use.
Document which agent may store which data class.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or compliance review.
